critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1273 lines (nearly 2x the 700-line threshold). Auth (setup + routes), Cantiere, Lavori, PDF generation, Backup/Restore, and Tariffe should be split into routers/services modules. Currently the auth block appears BEFORE routes and models which forces ordering constraints.

CORS misconfiguration risk: backend/.env has CORS_ORIGINS='*' AND middleware uses allow_credentials=True + expose_headers=['*']. Per fetch spec browsers reject Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* with credentials, so cross-origin cookie auth from a different domain would silently fail. It only works today because the frontend is served through the same preview domain (proxied /api). For future custom domains, replace '*' with an explicit list.

The startup handler _startup calls seed_admin() which references module-level `logger`, but `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is defined at line 1267 AFTER `_startup` registration. This currently works because startup fires after full module import, but it's fragile — move logger initialization to top of module.

JWT secret is stored in plain .env (good) but there is no key rotation strategy; tokens are HS256 with 8h TTL and no refresh token endpoint. If secret ever leaks, all sessions must be invalidated by rotating and forcing re-login. Consider a jti + revocation list in DB, or shorter TTL + refresh flow.
No brute-force lockout / rate limiting on /api/auth/login. Playbook guideline mentions lockout after 5 fails — not implemented. For a single-tenant admin app this is low risk, but flag as follow-up.
Password validation: /api/auth/register accepts ANY password length (even 1 char). Add min-length + complexity policy at Pydantic layer.

auth.jsx: `if (user && user !== false)` uses truthy check but user can be null (checking), false (guest), or object; explicit === object check would be clearer. Also login() sets user from response body but does NOT call check() so if backend adds fields (created_at etc.) they will be missing until reload — minor.
ProtectedRoute renders 'Caricamento…' during initial auth check but there is no timeout — if /auth/me hangs the user sees an infinite spinner. Add a 5-10s timeout to axios or auth check.

The bulk PDF export loads ALL clienti + serializes ALL PDFs synchronously in a single request. With 200 clients and current PDF sizes (~5-10KB each) the ZIP is small, but with logos+lavori history it could take >30s and hit ingress timeouts. Consider a background job pattern for scale.

Home page ('/') is NOT wrapped in Layout, so a user landing on '/' sees no sidebar / no logout button. To log out they must navigate to /dashboard first. Consider adding a compact user menu / logout button on Home too.
